analysis.title: USA: Goods Trade Deficit Widens More Than Expected in September
key_insights: The advance goods trade deficit widened by $2.8bn to $134.9bn in September (SA by GS), against expectations for a slight narrowing. GS had forecast -$130.0bn and the median forecast was -$130.2bn.
Goods exports rose $5.3bn to $209.2bn. Goods imports rose $8.1bn to $344.1bn, driven by a $10.9bn increase in capital goods imports, which include electronics related to the AI buildout.
Capital goods imports have been a primary contributor to the widening trade deficit this year. They have partially offset the effect of rapidly rising AI business investment on GDP growth.

The details of the advance economic indicators report were weaker on net than GS's previous GDP tracking assumptions. Faster-than-assumed inventory accumulation mechanically boosts growth, but the wider-than-expected goods trade deficit more than offset it.
GS will finalize its GDP tracking estimate later on 28 October in its usual preview.

macro_indicators.interpretation: The deficit widened by $2.8bn from a prior -$132.1bn, versus expectations of a slight narrowing. This is a drag on GDP tracking estimates, partly offset by faster inventory accumulation.
GS's own forecast. The actual print was $4.9bn wider.
Consensus expected a slight narrowing from the prior month. The actual print was $4.7bn wider.
Exports rose, but by less than the increase in imports.
Imports were driven by capital goods tied to the AI buildout.
A sharp increase in imports of capital goods, including AI-related electronics, which weighs on net trade in GDP.

risk_factors: A wider goods trade deficit driven by AI-related capital goods imports offsets the GDP contribution of AI business investment and weighs on growth tracking estimates.
